risks.title: Entire desktop/Steam shell and CI workflow exist only in the uncommitted working tree
risks.description: electron/main.cjs, package.json's desktop:* scripts and electron-builder config, build/ icons, .github/workflows/quality.yml, RELEASE_READINESS.md, STEAM_RELEASE.md, AppErrorBoundary.tsx, and buildInfo.ts are all untracked or modified-but-uncommitted. None of this survives `git clean -fd` / a lost working copy / a fresh clone.
risks.owner: user (per this audit's instructions, uncommitted work is user-owned and not to be altered)

risks.title: 333 of 361 exported 3D assets are unreachable at runtime
risks.description: Exhaustive grep of every assetLibrary.load()/assetUrl() call site in src/ shows only the 'world' domain (23/26 ids used) and one hardcoded airframe id ('hero_ultralight') are ever loaded. 69 of 70 airframe generations, all 19 upgrade models, and all 245 micro-asset models (air_mic/env_mic/vfx) sit in public/ fully exported, licensed, and dead. This was not previously called out in VISUAL_DEBT.md, meaning current visual-debt tracking undercounts the actual gap between spec-authored content (8 frame generations, spec section 24.1) and shipped-reachable content (1 frame).

risks.title: No device-profiled visual capture evidence exists (VIS-004, spec's own P0 release gate)
risks.description: VISUAL_DEBT.md marks VIS-004 as 'Open' with player visibility 'Release gate' and severity P0. VISUAL_STATE.md independently names this as the current bottleneck. No capture/profile evidence for target mobile hardware exists in the repo.

risks.title: Mobile payload: >1.2MB gzip of engine code (Rapier+Three) before any gameplay asset, on a mobile-first PWA
risks.description: Production build measured this audit: rapier chunk 1093.93 kB gzip, three.js 164.53 kB gzip. The spec's stated primary platform is 'navegador movil (iOS/Android), PWA instalable.' No lazy-loading of the physics/render engines was found; screens are already route-split but the engine bundle is not deferred past first flight load.

risks.title: Accessibility WCAG 2.2 AA target unverified beyond attribute presence
risks.description: aria-*/reduced-motion code exists in 12+ files, but RELEASE_READINESS.md requires an automated scan plus a manual audit of the custom flight HUD and virtual sticks -- neither has been run. Custom touch controls are exactly the kind of component automated scanners under-cover.

risks.title: Flight model realism/difficulty balance has zero external playtest data
risks.description: README explicitly self-flags this: deterministic unit tests cover takeoff/stall/recovery/landing, but no human playtest telemetry exists. Any marketing claim about difficulty or realism would currently be unsupported.
evidence: README.md 'What's stubbed / explicitly TODO' flight-model bullet

risks.title: All commercial/legal pre-publication work is unstarted
risks.description: Pricing, storefront copy, privacy policy, terms, age rating, jurisdiction disclosures, and formal asset-licensing sign-off are all listed as unstarted mandatory pre-publication items in RELEASE_READINESS.md and STEAM_RELEASE.md. None can be inferred or completed from repository state.
risks.owner: release owner (external to repo, per both docs' own framing)

risks.title: STEAM_RELEASE.md's smoke-test claim is undated/unreproduced by this audit
risks.description: STEAM_RELEASE.md states the macOS package 'has been smoke-tested locally' but gives no date and this audit deliberately did not re-run npm run desktop:package (long-running, mutates release/, out of scope for a planning-only pass). The claim should not be treated as current proof without a fresh, dated run.

risks.title: VIS-005 texture generation blocked on external vendor credits
risks.description: VISUAL_DEBT.md VIS-005: AI texture generation for a planned terrain tile cannot run because the configured provider has no remaining credits. Explicit instruction in the doc: do not substitute unreviewed art in the meantime.

risks.title: Doc/code drift: README claims 16 missions, code defines 17
risks.description: Minor but concrete evidence of documentation drift; worth checking whether other README claims (e.g. exact counts) have similarly drifted from src/content/*.ts as the campaign was extended.
